newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Oil FPSO order to go to Japan-Swiss group.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Oil FPSO order to go to Japan-Swiss group.

text.p: Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd said on Tuesday it has informally decided to award a contract to build a floating oil production facility to be used at its oilfield in Vietnam to a Japanese-Swiss consortium.
The consortium comprises Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd and Switzerland's Single Buoy Moorings Inc (SBM).

The construction cost has not been agreed upon between Mitsubishi Oil and the consortium, but it usually costs about 10 billion yen to manufacture a Floating Production, Storage and Offloading (FPSO) vessel with a storage capacity of 800,000 barrels, a spokesman for the Japanese oil firm said.
The FPSO vessel receives what is pumped from oil wells and separates crude oil from gas and water.
Mitsubishi Oil plans to start crude oil production at the Rang Dong prospect off southern Vietnam in May 1998, with daily output of around 45,000 barrels.
The FPSO will be developed by modifying an oil tanker, and Mitsubishi Oil will lease the vessel from the consortium, he said.
It is unclear when Mitsubishi Oil will formally award the construction contract to the consortium, he added.
